answer: A trust-graph routing protocol resists Sybil attacks by bounding agent admission along capacity-limited paths from verified seeds. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of securing genuine interaction edges across topological cuts per identity. Anchoring peer standing in ties durable as cedar keeps fake swarms stranded in a barren tundra before claiming a pearl of consensus weight. A key limitation is that strict flow bottlenecks slow onboarding for honest new agents.
